title: Oaken: Fast and Efficient LLM Serving with Online-Offline Hybrid KV Cache Quantization
problem: LLM serving with large batch sizes is bottlenecked by KV cache memory bandwidth and capacity: HBM provides high bandwidth but limited capacity, while high-capacity LPDDR memory lacks bandwidth. Existing KV cache quantization approaches either incur excessive online outlier detection overhead (e.g., topK sorting at O(n log n)) or sacrifice accuracy through coarse-grained grouping.
motivation: As LLM context lengths and serving batch sizes grow, the KV cache dominates memory usage and becomes the primary throughput bottleneck, making efficient quantization with low runtime overhead essential for cost-effective inference.
method: Oaken has two stages: offline, it runs about 100 inferences to find data-agnostic breakpoints (thresholds that depend only on the layer, not the input data) in values for each layer. Online during inference, these thresholds partition each token's KV data into three groups: large outliers, small outliers, and normal values. For each group, group-shift quantization subtracts the threshold to narrow the value range, then encodes each value with 4 or 5 bits. Outliers are fused into unused slots of the dense 4-bit matrix using 8 bits total per outlier, and a custom hardware engine with DMA and page-based memory management handles bandwidth-efficient burst access from HBM or LPDDR memory; the system is built on an LPU architecture synthesized in TSMC 28nm.
key_novelty: By pre-computing per-layer value thresholds offline, Oaken avoids expensive online sorting and can pack outliers directly into unused slots of the dense 4-bit matrix, reducing storage from 23 to 8 bits per outlier.
contributions: Online-offline hybrid KV cache quantization that avoids O(n log n) online sorting by using offline-profiled thresholds for three-group value partitioning
Group-shift quantization that narrows the value range of outlier groups to enable low-bitwidth uniform quantization without FP16 fallback
Fused dense-and-sparse encoding that embeds 5-bit outlier values into zeroed elements of the 4-bit dense matrix, reducing storage overhead by 65% vs. COO+FP16
Custom quantization/dequantization engines and page-based MMU integrated into DMA, achieving up to 1.58x throughput over A100 GPU with only 8.21% area overhead

metrics.speedup: 1.79x over vLLM, 1.58x over QServe at batch size 256
metrics.accuracy: 0.54% average accuracy loss vs. state-of-the-art KV quantization baselines
metrics.other: KV bitwidth reduction up to 70%; synthesized at TSMC 28nm

limitations: Offline profiling must be repeated per model, and the fixed group ratio (4%/90%/6%) may be suboptimal for models with highly atypical KV distributions.
primary_theme: Online-offline hybrid KV cache quantization for LLM serving
